name: El Niño
description: El Niño is a natural climate pattern in which parts of the tropical Pacific Ocean become unusually warm. It changes weather around the world, causing droughts in some places and heavier rain or flooding in others.
topic: Droughts and floods caused by El Niño and their impact on agriculture and livelihoods
data_filter: evidence related to these specific El Niño events in 1997-98, 2015-16, 2018-19, 2023-24, 2026-27

metrics.name: Cropland
metrics.description: Cultivated cropland affected by droughts or floods in every El Niño event since 1997 as a percentage of total area cultivated, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: More than 35% of cultivated land in the south was completely dry, with no harvest expected until the following rainy season.

metrics.name: Pastureland
metrics.description: Pastureland affected by droughts or floods in every El Niño event since 1997 as a percentage of total area pastured, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: More than 40% of pastureland in the north was completely dry, with no grazing expected until the following rainy season.

metrics.name: Crop yield loss
metrics.description: Crop yield loss as a result of droughts or floods during El Niño events since 1997 as a percentage of total crop yield, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: Among households surveyed in 14 affected districts, 51% reported harvests more than 50% lower than in 2023. Nearly 720,000 tonnes of maize were lost, valued at about USD 349 million and equivalent to roughly 7% of agricultural GDP

metrics.name: Livestock loss
metrics.description: Livestock loss as a result of droughts or floods during El Niño events since 1997 as a percentage of total livestock, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: In the worst-affected areas, over 30% of livestock were lost, amounting to an estimated USD 247 million in economic losses.

metrics.name: Damage to agriculture infrastructure
metrics.description: Damage to agriculture infrastructure or productive assets as a result of droughts or floods during El Niño events since 1997, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: Prolonged flooding damaged up to 80–95% of irrigated farms in some areas.

metrics.name: Change in livelihood
metrics.description: Change in livelihood or farming decision as a result of droughts or floods during El Niño events since 1997
metrics.example: Crop failure then forced more than half of the households surveyed to replant, while some were unable to do so because they lacked seeds or weather conditions remained unfavorable.Crop and income losses pushed some farming households to borrow money to purchase seed and meet basic needs, increasing debt and the risk of selling productive assets

metrics.name: Coping strategies
metrics.description: Farmers or pastoralists coping strategies to droughts or floods during El Niño events since 1997
metrics.example: 26% sold livestock to meet immediate needs, mainly food, while 25% consumed seed stocks intended for the next planting season

metrics.name: Subsequent hazards
metrics.description: Subsequent hazards that have an impact on agriculture during El Niño events since 1997
metrics.example: Drought was compounded by fall armyworm attacks on maize and other crops reported by surveyed households, illustrating that the agricultural consequences of an El Niño season are not confined to rainfall deficits alone. Drought impacts were compounded by pest outbreaks, including rat infestations, and affected rice, corn, vegetables and other crops.

metrics.name: Food prices
metrics.description: Food price increase as a result of drought or flood during El Niño events since 1997
metrics.example: Food prices were around 40% above the five-year average, while maize prices had more than doubled year-on-year

metrics.name: Supply and trade disruptions
metrics.description: Supply and trade disruption as a result of drought or flood during El Niño events since 1997
metrics.example: the country contracted a record 1.35 million tonnes of rice imports

metrics.name: Hunger
metrics.description: Incident of Hunger or food insecurity during El Niño events since 1997
metrics.example: Between April and September 2024, 2.79 million people faced IPC Phase 3 or worse acute food insecurity

metrics.name: Food insecurity impact
metrics.description: Projected impacts on food insecurity; food prices; hunger linked to El Nino 2026
metrics.example: Expectations of a decline in wheat output to a level below the five‑year average, as an increased likelihood of El Niño‑induced below‑average rainfall and elevated input costs are foreseen to curtail both plantings and yields.

metrics.name: Deaths and missing persons
metrics.description: How many people died or were reported missing due to climatological, hydrological, or meteorological hazards (contextual for El Niño-related impacts). DesInventar reports deaths and missing persons; EM-DAT reports total deaths. Impacts are linked to hazards (e.g. floods, drought), not El Niño itself.
metrics.example: Floods in Kenya caused deaths reported in DesInventar and EM-DAT.

metrics.name: People affected, injured and requiring assistance
metrics.description: How many people were affected, injured or required assistance due to climatological, hydrological, or meteorological hazards (contextual for El Niño-related impacts). EM-DAT reports injured, affected, and total affected; DesInventar reports injured, affected, and victims (damnificados). Impacts are linked to hazards (e.g. floods, drought), not El Niño itself.
metrics.example: 695,255 people were affected by floods in Kenya in 2023 (EM-DAT).

metrics.name: Displaced, evacuated and relocated people
metrics.description: How many people were displaced, evacuated or relocated due to climatological, hydrological, or meteorological hazards (contextual for El Niño-related impacts). DesInventar reports evacuated and relocated people; EM-DAT reports people whose homes were destroyed or heavily damaged and who need shelter (No. Homeless). Impacts are linked to hazards (e.g. floods, drought), not El Niño itself.
metrics.example: 650 people were relocated after floods in Turkana (DesInventar); EM-DAT also reports people left homeless.

metrics.name: Housing damaged and destroyed
metrics.description: How many houses were damaged or destroyed, and associated reconstruction, insured, and total damage costs, due to climatological, hydrological, or meteorological hazards (contextual for El Niño-related impacts). DesInventar reports houses destroyed and damaged; EM-DAT reports people needing shelter (No. Homeless) and CPI-adjusted damage costs. Impacts are linked to hazards (e.g. floods, drought), not El Niño itself.
metrics.example: Floods destroyed and damaged houses in DesInventar records; EM-DAT reports people left homeless and adjusted total damage.

metrics.name: Education and health facilities affected
metrics.description: How many education and health facilities were affected due to climatological, hydrological, or meteorological hazards (contextual for El Niño-related impacts). DesInventar reports counts of schools and hospitals affected. Impacts are linked to hazards (e.g. floods, drought), not El Niño itself.
metrics.example: Landslides damaged schools recorded in DesInventar.

metrics.name: Roads, bridges, energy, water and communications affected
metrics.description: How infrastructure was affected (roads, energy, water, sewerage, and communications) due to climatological, hydrological, or meteorological hazards (contextual for El Niño-related impacts). DesInventar reports kilometres of roads affected and sector flags for transport, energy, water, sewerage, and communications. Impacts are linked to hazards (e.g. floods, drought), not El Niño itself.
metrics.example: Floods disrupted water supply and communications in DesInventar event records.
